integration_questions: Does the slalom progress move past the 0.16 to 0.20 plateau with a controller change alone, which would confirm the stall is controller reaction time rather than geometry?
Does steering_oscillation on the oval stay at or below about 0.25 with the 0.10 m body, or does the lower yaw inertia add jitter the controller must damp?
Are line_loss_events on the s-bend still near 1 per run at bend entries, and does control_effort stay within 5 to 9?
Is there any controller-side reason (for example kd or the line-loss setting) that would let the robot use the 0.10 m body's faster turn response without going off track?

intent: Final iteration: consolidate on the best-evidenced geometry (iteration 10, score 450.6) rather than test an untried change on the unseen-track race. The geometry is unchanged, so the Integrator's controller work is tuned on the platform that has the strongest evidence. Expected result: about 450 on the development tracks, with 20/20 oval finishes and s-bend progress near 0.6.
learning: Across ten iterations, the robust gains came from forward sensors at y=0.08 m, a 0.012 m footprint, a radius-to-track ratio near 0.40, and a shorter body. Sensing and span changes that widened or enlarged the footprint hurt. Mass 0.5 kg hurt. Slalom progress did not respond to any geometry lever, so the next gains are probably controller-side.
rationale: Ten races are on record, and iteration 10 is the best design so far (score 450.6, up from 417.9 in iteration 8). Its geometry is: 5 sensors at y=0.08 m spanning ±0.03 m at 0.015 m pitch, 0.012 m footprint, wheel_track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.040 m, mass 0.6 kg, body_length 0.10 m, body_width 0.12 m. Its oval finishes 20/20 with rms_error 0.0195, and its s-bend finishes 3/20 with progress 0.61, up from 0.66 in iteration 8 with a finish time of 2.12 s. The shorter body cut yaw inertia and produced the largest single gain of the recent sweep. The sensing, row-position, track, radius and mass levers have each been tested in at least one direction. Footprint 0.016 m collapsed the oval, 0.008 m hurt the s-bend, and 0.012 m is the optimum. The row is already at the y=0.08 m limit. Mass 0.5 kg hurt, and 0.6 kg is the better value. Slalom progress has stayed at 0.16 to 0.20 under every change, so the slalom stall looks like a controller reaction-time limit rather than a geometry limit. This is the final iteration, and any untested geometry change carries real risk to the unseen-track race. Changing wheel_radius to 0.045 m or narrowing track further would be speculative: the radius-to-track ratio and speed trade-off are untested beyond 0.040 m, and the s-bend already showed sensitivity to ratio. I therefore propose to resubmit the iteration 10 geometry unchanged. The robot that races is the one with the strongest evidence, and the Integrator can tune the controller on it. Expected result: about 450 on the development tracks, with the same oval reliability and the same s-bend behaviour.
